judgments.reasoning_cat1: Investment of the Swap Account is to be made 'at the direction of the Majority Class CE Certificateholder' but the default rule turns on 'the absence of written instructions to the Securities Administrator', so it is unclear who must be instructed and by whom; the account is also said to be maintained by the Swap Administrator elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It provides that the Supplemental Interest Trust 'shall hold the Swap Agreement, the Swap Administration Agreement ... and the Swap Account', which contradicts the Trust Fund definition (c335) that includes the rights under the Swap Administration Agreement in the Trust Fund; it also remits amounts 'in the manner provided in clause (e) below', a clause the Section's lettering does not obviously reach.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanically clear but circular in its tax fiction — amounts paid to senior Holders are 'treated as distributed to the Class CE Certificateholders ... and paid by' them — and the fund established by the Securities Administrator is titled in the Trustee's name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the provision that actually establishes the Reserve Fund and requires the Reserve Fund Deposit, directly contradicting the Reserve Fund and Reserve Fund Deposit definitions (c283, c284), which say both are created and made 'pursuant to Section 6.08 hereof'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Extremely long parentheticals repeated verbatim make the payment priority hard to follow, and the provision breaks off mid-sentence ('subordinated to distributions to the Holders of the Class A, Class M and Class'), so the subordination limb is incomplete as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Class IO Distribution Amount definition (c075) says the amount equals what is payable under 'the first and second sentences of Section 4.22(c)' in excess of the amount payable on REMIC VI Regular Interest IO, while this subsection describes the deeming in its third sentence — the sentence-count reference does not match.
